title: Console: Auto-rollback event detail panel for rollouts (why/metrics/actions)
creator: Kenji Nakamura
description:
Goal
Design the Rollout Timeline “event detail panel” for auto actions (auto-pause, auto-rollback, suppressed) triggered by SLO breach evaluation. The panel must make it easy for oncall/service owners to understand:
- what happened (action + scope)
- why it happened (decision explanation + policy thresholds)
- what signals it used (metrics snapshot summary + monitor IDs)
- what to do next (safe actions + links)

Context
Auto-mitigation is a reliability differentiator for Redwood rollouts. When an SLO breach triggers an automatic action, operators must be able to trust the decision, validate monitors quickly, and have clear next steps. We also need to handle “non-ideal” states cleanly (monitor missing/stale, suppressed due to incident, insufficient sample size) without confusing users.

Primary users
- SRE / oncall responders (triage + mitigation)
- Service owners / platform engineers (debug rollout regressions)
- Release engineers (validate readiness and enablement)

Non-goals
- Designing the policy editor (see DES-951)
- Rebuilding full metrics dashboards (we link out)
- Incident management flows (we integrate with existing runbooks/Slack)

Where this UI lives
Console → Rollouts → Rollout details → Timeline
- Clicking an auto-action event opens a right-side detail panel (or modal on small screens)
- Panel supports deep-linking via URL fragment/query (for sharing in Slack/oncall)

Event types to support (MVP)
1) Auto action executed
- Auto-rollback executed (traffic shifted back to baseline / previous version)
- Auto-pause executed (rollout step halted)

2) Auto action suppressed / not executed
- Suppressed (explicit admin override or incident suppression window)
- No action due to guardrails (insufficient sample size, debounce/holdoff not satisfied)
- Missing/stale monitor (policy wanted evaluation but monitor data unavailable)

Panel information architecture (proposed)
A) Header
- Title: "Auto-rollback executed" | "Auto-pause executed" | "Auto-rollback suppressed" | "Auto action not taken"
- Status pill: Executed / Suppressed / No action
- Timestamp (with timezone) + “evaluated window” (e.g., fast burn 5m, slow burn 30m)
- Scope chips (clickable): Route, Model version, Region, Customer tier
- Correlation identifiers (expand/copy): rollout_id, decision_id, audit_event_id

B) “Why” summary (human readable)
Single sentence + expandable details. Examples:
- Executed: “p95 latency burned 6.2× budget over 5m (threshold 4×) and 2.3× over 30m (threshold 2×); rollback policy v12 triggered.”
- Paused: “Error rate breached fast-burn threshold; rollout paused at step 3/6 per policy.”
- Suppressed: “Breach detected but action suppressed: active incident override ‘telemetry-outage-2026-02-17’.”
- No action: “Breach signal detected but minimum sample size not met (needs 5k req / 5m; observed 812).”

C) Metrics snapshot summary
Compact, scannable cards with “as of” time:
- Latency: p95, p99 (ms) + delta vs baseline (if available)
- Error rate: 5xx% (or “non-2xx”) + count
- Saturation (optional): GPU queue depth / utilization signal used
- Burn rate: fast/slow value + threshold
- Sample size: requests, tokens (if available), duration covered

Design notes:
- Show “Used in decision” checkmark per metric (some policies may evaluate only error rate)
- For each metric, include a “View chart” link that opens the pre-filtered dashboard (route/model/region/tier + time range around event)

D) Policy + monitors
- Policy section
  - Policy name/template (e.g., “Dedicated: Conservative rollback”) and policy version
  - Action configured on breach: rollback | pause | shift traffic to baseline
  - Guardrails: debounce/holdoff, min sample size, max actions per hour (if available)
- Monitors section
  - List monitor IDs/names queried (latency, error) with status: OK/BREACH/STALE/MISSING
  - “Open monitor definition” (RBAC gated for some tenants)
  - If multiple monitors: show which one(s) triggered breach

E) Decision trace (advanced / collapsible)
For oncall + debugging. Should be collapsible by default.
- Evaluation timeline: “Fast window breached at T-2m; slow window breached at T-1m; holdoff satisfied; executor succeeded”
- Links: audit log event, metrics snapshot reference, runbook section
- Executor details (for executed actions): “traffic shift: 30%→0% over 2m in 6 steps; idempotency token …” (only if available from audit schema; otherwise hide)

F) Actions (contextual)
Always available:
- View dashboards (opens metrics dashboard with recommended time range)
- Copy link to this event
- View runbook (deep link to “Auto-rollback triage” section)

When action executed:
- “Re-attempt rollout” (if the rollout is in paused/rolled back state and user has permission) → routes to existing rollout controls, not implemented here, but we must define placement and handoff.
- “Open incident” (optional future; for MVP we can link to incident process doc)

When suppressed:
- “View suppression details” (who/why/expiry)
- If admin: “Edit suppression” / “End suppression” (admin-only; should include a confirmation and require a reason)

When missing/stale:
- “Diagnose monitor” (links to runbook + monitor coverage guidance)
- If admin/service owner: “Request monitor setup” (creates a prefilled internal ticket) — optional; if too heavy for MVP, omit and only show guidance.

Edge cases & UX behavior
1) Missing monitor
- Panel must not imply rollback was prevented by healthy metrics; it should clearly state “insufficient monitoring data”.
- Copy:
  - Title: “Auto action not taken (monitor missing)”
  - Why summary: “Policy requires SLO monitor(s), but no eligible monitor was found for this scope.”
  - Provide guidance and link to coverage audit/runbook.

2) Stale monitor / metric lag
- Show “STALE” with last datapoint timestamp and staleness threshold (if provided).
- Recommended UI: warning banner at top: “Monitor data is stale; decision may be delayed.”

3) Suppressed due to incident
- Show banner: “Suppressed during incident” with incident identifier, suppression start/end, and actor.
- Ensure users can still view metrics snapshot and monitor state.

4) Guardrails prevented action
- Provide explicit guardrail reason(s): min sample not met, debounce not met, max actions per hour reached.
- Avoid blame-y language; focus on safety: “Guardrail active to prevent oscillation.”

5) Partial data availability
- If latency monitor available but error monitor missing (or vice versa), panel must show which signals were evaluated vs skipped.

6) Multi-tenant / RBAC
- Some actions/links should be admin-only:
  - edit/end suppression
  - view raw monitor definitions (depending on internal vs customer)
- For non-admins, show disabled buttons with tooltip: “Admin permission required (RolloutAutoMitigation:Override)”.

Content/copy requirements
- Keep the top summary readable in <10 seconds.
- Use consistent terms across Console + runbook: “auto-rollback”, “auto-pause”, “suppressed”, “monitor stale”, “minimum sample size”.
- Include a short “What this means” help text for customer-facing views (Hosted/Dedicated customers), but avoid revealing internal monitor IDs if not allowed.

Deliverables
- Figma: component spec for the detail panel (desktop + mobile), including empty/loading/error states.
- Copy deck: strings for each event type + edge case states.
- Interaction spec: deep-link behavior, keyboard focus, and how links open (new tab vs same tab).

Open questions
- Do we always have baseline comparison available for latency delta? If not, design should gracefully omit “delta vs baseline”.
- Should we show token-level info (tokens/sec, prompt vs generation) in MVP? (Likely no; link out to runtime dashboards.)
- Do we expose monitor IDs to customers, or only “monitor name”? Needs security review alignment.

Acceptance criteria
- A user can answer: what happened, why, and what to do next from the panel without leaving the Rollout page (dashboards are optional).
- Panel supports the following states with clear messaging: executed rollback, executed pause, suppressed, no action (guardrail), missing monitor, stale monitor.
- Actions are correctly RBAC gated and don’t create unsafe one-click flows.

References
- Confluence: ADR-0128 (audit schema), runbook (triage steps), observability standards (metric naming)
- Linear: ENG-4833 (timeline UI), ENG-4831 (API)
- Known pain: postmortem “monitor missing/stale prevented mitigation” (Feb 2026)
comments: 2026-02-12 (Alicia Perez): Drafted IA and state matrix. Biggest risk is confusing “no action” due to missing monitor vs “healthy”; proposing a dedicated top banner for missing/stale so it’s unmissable.

2026-02-13 (Sean Gallagher): +1 on banner. Please include explicit sample size + last datapoint timestamp. Also need copy to discourage folks from disabling suppression without verifying telemetry health.
2026-02-14 (Marissa Cole): PM preference: default collapsed “Decision trace” to keep panel approachable. Make sure “View dashboards” is prominent and pre-filters by rollout scope.
2026-02-18 (Kenji Nakamura): Added note on mobile behavior (modal). Please spec deep-linking; we want Slack notifications to jump directly to the event detail.
2026-02-21 (Felix Schneider): From eng side, we will have audit_event_id, policy_version, and a list of evaluated monitors. Baseline delta may be missing initially—design should treat it as optional.
2026-02-25 (Kevin Osei): For customer-facing consoles, avoid exposing internal monitor IDs; prefer display names and a generic “monitor reference”. Admin-only can see IDs.
